info.title: frontend-contract
info.description: Async API with versioned references, background tasks, private media, and observability.

get.description: Recipient-only SSE invalidations over the persisted unified inbox. Requires an active bearer access token, user, session and registered client. No query parameters or user_id are accepted. Native EventSource needs an authenticated Node proxy; direct clients use streaming fetch with Authorization. Subscribe then refresh inbox/search and inbox/unread on inbox.resync, on reconnect and at least every 60 seconds. Last-Event-ID is an optional bounded reconnect hint, not an authorized replay cursor. inbox.changed contains only schema_version and notification_ref_id; its SSE id is the same reference. Deduplicate ids and coalesce refreshes. No subject, business data, password, URL or error is streamed. Heartbeat and authorization checks have a 15-second cadence; authorization probes are bounded to 3 seconds and changed events recheck authorization before sending. A stream lasts at most 300 seconds, receives at most 256 signals, and times out blocked sends after 5 seconds. Limit 3 streams per recipient and 200 per configured cache namespace across processes. No stream-long database session. Offline/missed signals remain in persisted search. Authentication or service failure after headers closes the stream; pre-stream errors use existing JSON envelopes. Success is text/event-stream, never a JSON success envelope. Private no-store/no-transform; proxies must disable buffering/compression and propagate disconnects. This backend contract does not establish browser or Node proxy acceptance.

parameters.description: Optional preferred response language. English and Farsi are supported; regional tags use their base language and unsupported values fall back to English.

parameters.description: Optional UUIDv7 correlation identifier. Missing or invalid values are replaced with a generated UUIDv7; the effective value is returned in X-Request-ID.

parameters.description: Optional caller-supplied reason recorded in audit history. It is not an authorization credential.

200.description: Private SSE invalidations and heartbeat comments; no JSON envelope.

X-Client-Date-Status.description: Optional client Date reading: available, unavailable, or invalid. No request is rejected for this diagnostic.

X-Client-Date-Delta-Seconds.description: Signed server receipt minus client Date in seconds; includes transit and generation delay, so it is not exact clock skew.

X-Client-Date-Advisory.description: Present as check-device-time only when the configured apparent difference threshold is reached.

X-Server-Received-At.description: Server UTC receipt timestamp. Response Date, when present, is generated by the HTTP server or proxy.

post.description: Authenticated recipient-only unified inbox version 1. Case, work_item, ai_approval, report and account destinations resolve current owner-authorized references on every read. Calendar/support/operation targets are reserved and unavailable until their producers exist. An unavailable, deleted, revoked, expired or cancelled target exposes no private subject, content or reference. Stored labels never confer authority. Search is bounded and deterministic with existing filters/order/page/size plus unread=true/false; report is the same paginated search, not a queued archive. Unread totals count live ACTIVE unread inbox rows, including redacted unavailable destinations. Mark-read changes only read metadata, requires a current optimistic ref (409 when stale), and never decides or acts on a workflow. Non-owned refs fail 403; missing/deleted refs fail 404. Null read bodies are rejected; actions accept an empty object. UTC timestamps; en/fa template locale is chosen when staged with en fallback. Private no-store success/page envelopes, existing 401/403/404/409/422 errors. Refresh refs from mutation responses. Optional email defaults off; mandatory notices ignore optional opt-out. No delivery is performed by these reads.
